Subject: Implementation cadence: batching & routing calibration for NebulaDocs

Hi Ava / Sanjay —

Following our onboarding call, wanted to put a concise implementation cadence on email so we have alignment before we start profiling traffic next week. Goal: get NebulaDocs to target P95 latency <250ms for typical editor flows while reducing per-token cost through batching, KV caching, and a controlled quantization rollout.

High-level plan (proposed):
- Discovery (Nov 13–15): gather traffic samples, typical seq lengths, cold vs warm request ratios, and any QoS constraints.
- Profiling & baseline runs (Nov 16–17): run short batch-size sweep and KV-cache experiments against a staging snapshot of your workload.
- Canary (Nov 18–20): enable routing policy for 10% traffic to quantized variant + cache priming; monitor cost/latency/quality metrics and rollback rules.
- Rollout & tune (Nov 23–Dec 3): increase quantized traffic in steps; finalize batching config and TTLs.

What we need from you before Monday:
1) A 1–2 hour sample of production-like traffic (anonymized) or a representative CSV (timestamp, seq_len, prompt_type).
2) Access to a minimal telemetry endpoint (read-only) or a short CloudWatch/GCP Stackdriver export.
3) Any hard SLOs / disallowed failure modes (e.g., token-level hallucination tolerance thresholds).

I attached the onboarding cadence doc and a simple profiling template to fill in. Monica will own the experiments and will share specific knobs we will iterate on (batch size, max latency window, KV prefetch TTL, quant profiles). Karthik will be on-call for any routing changes in staging. Marissa will own customer updates/communication.

Propose a 30m sync Monday 11/16 10:00–10:30 PT to kick off the profiling run. If that works I will send an invite.

Thanks —
Rachel

Hey Ava / Sanjay —

Thanks for the sample — it looks representative. Quick responses to your Qs plus an engineering plan we will run during the profiling window.

Recommended defaults (initial):
- Batch sizing: start with dynamic batching enabled, target batch timeout 10ms, max batch size 12. In our experience that balances throughput without spiking tail latency for seq lengths <= 512.
- KV prefetch TTL: initial TTL 30s with active priming on warm requests; if your warm ratio >60% we will increase to 90s during canary.
- Quantization profile: start with INT8 (symmetric) as the primary profile and an INT4-reduced profile behind a canary. Quality check: automated token-diff and sample-based human eval of 200 critical prompts.
- Routing policy (canary): 90% baseline model, 10% quantized variant. Auto-fallback enabled for any request that exceeds latency threshold or fails quality checks.

Profiling experiments (Nov 16–17):
1) Baseline collection: run 2 x 30m baseline traffic captures (no batching change) to get median P50/P95 and cost-per-1k tokens.
2) Batch sweep: run 4x 15m jobs varying max batch size [4,8,12,16] with dynamic timeout = 10ms to measure latency/cost curve.
3) KV primer test: enable KV prefetch TTL=30s and measure hit-rate and cold-warm delta for 1 hour.
4) Quant micro-canary: spin up quantized replica and route 1% synthetic traffic to check correctness and perf (no customer traffic yet).

Canary plan (Nov 18 start):
- Step 1 (Day 0–1): 1% real traffic to quantized + primed cache; monitor token-diff fail rate (target <0.5%) and P95 latency delta (target <+40ms).
- Step 2 (Day 2–3): 10% traffic if metrics stable. Run 200-sample human eval daily.
- Rollback criteria: token-diff >1% or P95 latency increase >100ms for 30m window -> immediate rollback to 0% and investigate.

Estimated cost impact: based on your sample, moving 10% to INT8 should reduce per-token spend for that slice by ~18–25% (depends on sequence length and padding). We will produce a short runbook with exact numbers after the profiling jobs.

Security / SOC2 evidence: Marissa, I can own the SOC2 artifacts list and will coordinate on the evidence request from NebulaDocs' security team.

Next steps I will take after the Monday call:
- Upload profiling job configs and the expected result CSV to the Drive link Rachel shared.
- Kick off baseline run Nov 16 11:00 PT.
- Add a lightweight Grafana dashboard for P50/P95, token-diff, cache hit-rate, and cost delta.

If everything looks good we will start the 1% quant micro-canary on Nov 18 morning PT.

Onward —
Monica Patel
